subject: PO pre-authorization, invoicing cadence & packaging constraints
messages:
From: Sasha Petrov <sasha.petrov@deephealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@deephealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PO requirements + invoice cadence question for Redwood engagement

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week — DeepHealth's procurement group asked me to confirm a few operational constraints before we issue a PO. High level we are ready to move but need clarity on:

- PO format: our ERP requires a PO number on each invoice and a specific PO header (vendor tax id, ship-to entity, BU code). Can you confirm Redwood accepts these as line-level fields?
- Invoice cadence: we prefer weekly invoice runs (consolidated weekly statement) for ongoing usage vs monthly. Is that supported?
- Net terms: our standard is Net45, but we can extend to Net60 if a discount is applied.
- Packaging/sku mapping: we bill usage to multiple business units; can one single contract be split across multiple GL codes (we'd like per-invoice BU code).
- Pre-authorized PO/purchase memo: procurement can provide a pre-authorized multiline PO with a spend cap; we need Redwood to honor the preauth and accept incremental weekly invoices against it.

I've attached our standard PO form for reference (DeepHealth_PO_Form_2026.pdf). Can you confirm what's feasible and whether there are any packaging/discount requirements we should be aware of? Also please indicate if you need any additional vendor setup docs for our AP team.

Appreciate a quick read — procurement wants to lock terms by end of week.

Best,
Sasha Petrov
Director, Strategic Sourcing
DeepHealth Inc.

Attachment: DeepHealth_PO_Form_2026.pdf (pdf)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Petrov <sasha.petrov@deephealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO requirements + invoice cadence question for Redwood engagement

Hi Sasha — thanks, and great to hear procurement is close. Quick answers up front, then a couple of asks so we can align the final PO language.

- PO fields: We can accept PO numbers and the standard header fields on each invoice. We map vendor fields into our billing system and can include a BU/GL code per invoice line if your AP requires it.
- Invoice cadence: Weekly consolidated statements are supported; we'll need the PO to specify the invoice cadence and the maximum cap for the preauthorized total.
- Net terms & discount: Standard Hosted customers are on Net30. For Net45/Net60 we typically require a pricing concession (we can offer a temporary volume discount or a one-time credit). Please share expected monthly run-rate so I can propose an approved concession range.
- Pre-authorized PO: We can accept an umbrella preauth PO that invoices draw against, provided the PO references the Redwood contract and a maximum spend cap.

I've attached our Billing PO template (redwood_PO_template_v2.pdf) — if you can populate the vendor fields and estimated monthly spend, that will speed legal/AP processing.

Propose next steps:
1) You send back a completed DeepHealth_PO_Form with estimated monthly spend and BU codes.
2) I'll circulate a proposed concession (discount %) for Net45/Net60 to the finance team and confirm whether we can accept weekly invoices under the preauth.

If budget allows, we could offer a 12% volume discount for the first quarter as a bridge for Net45 terms; I'll need sign-off from Billing. Is that an acceptable starting point?

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0176

Attachment: redwood_PO_template_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: PO requirements + invoice cadence question for Redwood engagement

Vanessa / Ben — forwarding Sasha's procurement questions from DeepHealth. Key points for finance approval:

- DeepHealth wants weekly invoice runs against a pre-authorized umbrella PO.
- They prefer Net45 (or Net60 with a discount). Mateo suggested a 12% volume discount for Q1 as a bridge to Net45.
- They require BU/GL per invoice line and PO header fields mapped into their ERP.
- Estimated monthly run-rate TBD — request they return the completed PO form.

Ben: is weekly invoicing against a preauth PO operationally acceptable? Any implications for reconciliation or remittance timing we should flag to the customer?
Vanessa: pricing side — is 12% for the first quarter acceptable under our current enterprise concession guidelines? If not, what's the approved range for a $50k-$150k/month customer?

Quote from Sasha's note: "our standard is Net45, but we can extend to Net60 if a discount is applied."

Thanks — I want to get back to procurement by EOD Friday.

--Mateo

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO requirements + invoice cadence question for Redwood engagement

Hi Mateo — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the template. Procurement reviewed and we can confirm the following:

- We'll populate your template and return the completed PO by Monday.
- DeepHealth is comfortable with weekly invoice runs drawn against a preauthorized umbrella PO as long as each invoice includes the PO number and BU code.
- Regarding terms: we reviewed internally and can accept Net45 with a 10%-12% discount band for an initial three-month period. We'll target 12% but can accept 10% if needed.
- Estimated monthly run-rate: preliminary estimate is $85k/mo across three business units (will detail in the PO).

Request: please confirm whether Redwood can invoice weekly with Net45 payment terms (payment due 45 days from invoice date) and that the 12% Q1 discount will be applied to invoiced amounts rather than as a post-invoice credit. Also, if there are any special invoice fields you require (e.g., Redwood vendor tax id format), let me know so our AP can populate correctly.

If that aligns, procurement will route the signed PO and we can kick off onboarding.

Thanks,
Sasha
Director, Strategic Sourcing
DeepHealth Inc.
